clue.text: A hold-up on the tennis court

parts.words: A hold-up on the tennis court
parts.note: a serve that clips the top of the barrier across a tennis court is held up and replayed

explanation.surface: A robbery taking place at a tennis club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold-up' suggests a robbery; here it is the tape at the top of the net, which holds the net up and can delay a serve as a let.
explanation.definitionFit: The band along the top of a tennis net literally holds it up, and a serve clipping it stops play.

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus standing on one point is the lozenge figure on playing cards.

explanation.definitionFit: Paying immediately in cash settles a debt without delay, while the prompter's wage is pay for giving cues.

clue.text: Genial potman's place in the Midlands

explanation.walkthrough: Royal Leamington Spa is a Warwickshire town in the English Midlands, famous for its spring waters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Warwickshire spa town lies in central England.

clue.text: As you see, they're useful, but no good for drinking

definitions.text: As you see, they're useful, but no good for drinking

parts.words: As you see, they're useful, but no good for drinking
parts.note: eyewear helps you see, but frameless lenses have no rim, so a drinking vessel of that kind would spill

explanation.surface: A remark about some odd vessels that look handy yet fail at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glasses' has two senses: spectacles to see with and tumblers to drink from. Spectacles with no frame round the lenses are useful for seeing, but a tumbler with no rim would be no use.
explanation.definitionFit: Frameless spectacles have lenses without any surrounding edge, which helps vision but would ruin a tumbler.
